newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo talks in Gabon on Sunday without main players.
newsitem.headline: Congo talks in Gabon on Sunday without main players.

text.p: Congo peace talks will take place in Gabon on Sunday with envoys of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor, Denis Sassou Nguesso, mediator and Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas said on Saturday.

Kolelas told reporters that the envoys would have power to take decisions but that the meeting would be a prelude to one between the two leaders, whose forces have been at the centre of over a week of bloody ethnic and political clashes.
"The two parties will send plenipotentiaries -- four for President Lissouba, four for President Sassou and four or five for the mediation committee," Kolelas said.
Gabon's veteran president Omar Bongo would chair the talks.
Kolelas said the aim had been to bring Lissouba and Sassou Nguesso together in person but problems with people ensuring Sassou Nguesso's security had complicated that process.
The fighting began on June 5 after the army surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home as part of a crackdown on private militias and unauthorised arms in the runup to a July 27 election.

The United States, France and the U.N. have thrown their weight behind efforts to end the showdown. The U.S. ambassadors attended all-party talks at the French ambassador's residence on Saturday. Kolelas made his announcement after that meeting.
U.N. and Organisation of African Unity special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun arrived and said that the idea of an African force in Brazzaville had not been ruled out.

"We are going to discuss this issue (with Lissouba, Sassou Nguesso and Kolelas). Then we have a meeting in Libreville with plenipotentiaries representing different movements so we can formalise this idea...we don't rule out an African presence," Sahnoun told reporters.
Despite sporadic firing in the centre of the former French colony's capital, a truce showed signs of taking hold.
